origin.description: Return the start and end of every match. A string with no match contributes a matrix with no rows.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares literal text, coll uses collation, and boundary matches character, word, line, or sentence boundaries. The empty string is a character boundary.

origin.details: Recycling and names follow str_locate. The empty pattern and boundary() both locate every boundary segment. Matches do not overlap. A miss is omitted rather than stored as a missing row. A zero-length match has an end smaller than its start.
origin.value: A list of integer matrices, one for each element of string or pattern. Each matrix has columns start and end and one row for each match.

translation.description: Return the start and end of every match. A string with no match contributes an empty list of rows.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, regex, and boundary return Pattern objects and select that engine. The empty string is a character boundary.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. pattern_type chooses the engine and pattern_opts supplies the stringi option list. Empty and bound both call stri_locate_all_boundaries. The other engines call stri_locate_all_fixed, stri_locate_all_coll, or stri_locate_all_regex. Every call passes omit_no_match=True. Names on string are kept when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string.
translation.value: A list of location matrices. Each matrix is a list of [start, end] rows. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. A missing position is stringi._na.NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.locate import str_locate_all
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
print(str_locate_all(fruit, "a"))
